findings.title: GUI single scans are filed with CORRECTED pixels labelled as raw; Save As and the full-resolution view then flat-field them a second time
findings.evidence: session.py:1441 `image, meta = self._scanner.scan(... keep_raw=True,)` then 1456 `self._file(seq, 0, image, meta, job.notes, tuple(job.tags) + ("gui",), mono=..., mono_channel=...)` -- no raw_image. FrameWriter 1089-1092: `raw_image = job.get("raw_image")` / `entry = library.save(job["image"] if raw_image is None else raw_image, ...)`. library.save records `"corrections_applied": list(corrections or [])` (empty). library.corrected: `image, report = apply_shading(image, record["reference"], record["ccd_mask"])`. Compare _prescan (1415) which does pass `raw_image = getattr(self._scanner, "last_pixels_raw", None)`.
findings.description: DirectScanner.scan returns the flat-fielded image and keeps the raw one in last_pixels_raw. ScanSession._scan never hands the raw pixels to _file, so FrameWriter files the corrected array as scan.tif while the record says nothing was baked in and shading.npz sits beside it. This is exactly the failure CLAUDE.md describes for the 26 prescans, but on every GUI single scan, and no test covers it.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator presses Scan at 1800 dpi. library/<id>/scan.tif holds corrected pixels with corrections_applied=[]. The full-resolution view (_load_full) and Save As/Save all/Export call library.corrected(), which divides by the reference again: edge columns are over-gained and clip, and the delivered file is not the picture that was shown. `make reconstruct` reports 'decode CHANGED ~99% of samples' for every GUI scan, drowning real regressions.
findings.recommendation: In _scan pass raw_image=getattr(self._scanner, 'last_pixels_raw', None) (as _prescan does). In FrameWriter/library.save refuse or pass corrections=['shading'] when raw_image is missing but meta['shading'] is set. Add a session test asserting scan.tif equals the scanner's raw pixels. Repair existing entries with `tools/library.py migrate-raw --write` (their raw.bin.gz is correct).

findings.title: Calibration bytes are thrown away; the stored shading.npz cannot be recomputed with newer code
findings.evidence: calibrate_shading(... keep_data: bool = False); `data = b"".join(collected)` / `self._shading = calculate_shading(data, width)` / `"data": data if keep_data else None`. ensure_shading calls `result = self.calibrate_shading()` with no keep_data. library.save only does `reference.save(path / "shading.npz")`.
findings.description: The reference is a derived product of calculate_shading's level-based split (split_ratio 5.0, widest-gap cut) and averaging. The ~1.66 MB of calibration lines, the shading descriptor, the 128-byte calibration-info block, the calibration pass's own CCD mask and the gain/offset readbacks are only logged. Every entry therefore stores the output of today's shading-analysis code rather than the bytes it came from, which contradicts the owner's requirement and library.py's claim that raw.bin.gz is the ground truth everything else derives from.
findings.failure_scenario: A better dark/light split or outlier rejection is written next year. No entry can be re-corrected with it, because the lines it would need were never written; the reference also cannot be audited when a column artefact is suspected to come from the split.
findings.recommendation: Always keep the calibration bytes; store them once per calibration (e.g. library/calibrations/<sha256>.bin.gz with descriptor, info block, mask, gain readbacks, resolution, time) and reference that sha from every entry's calibration block. Let library.corrected optionally rebuild the reference from those bytes.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/library.py:21-26: '`raw.bin.gz` is the ground truth and everything else is derived from it'

findings.title: Roll frames and bracket passes lose their metering evidence and are recorded as commanded (exposure_metered=False)
findings.evidence: scan_roll: `scales = self.auto_exposure(target=exposure_target, infrared=infrared, film=film)` then `image, meta = self.scan(..., exposure_scale=scales, ...)` (no auto_exposure). scan(): `"exposure_metered": bool(auto_exposure),` and `if auto_exposure and self.last_metering is not None: meta["metering"] = self.last_metering`. scan_bracket does the same (2376 then 2392).
findings.description: Metering happens outside scan() on the roll and bracket paths, so meta never gets 'metering' and every frame claims its exposure was asked for. The roll is the main production path (meter='each' default), so the per-probe levels/targets/limits exist nowhere durable.
findings.failure_scenario: A 38-frame colour-negative roll: no library entry has scan.metering; BLUE_RGBI_HEADROOM cannot be checked from ordinary work; a frame that came out dark cannot be told from one metered against an odd frame; library.signature treats metered exposures as commands.
findings.recommendation: Have scan_roll/scan_bracket attach `meta['metering']=self.last_metering` and set exposure_metered True (or a 'metered_by' field) for the frames whose scales came from auto_exposure; with meter='once' reference the first frame's metering.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/direct.py:2026-2030 'What each round measured is left on last_metering, and scan files it with the entry'; direct.py:358-360 'last_metering records blue's achieved level on every metered scan'

findings.title: Debug filing attaches a previous pass's raw bytes (or none) to any pass that did not ask keep_raw
findings.evidence: read_planes: `if keep_raw: self.last_raw = blob; self.last_raw_layout = {...}` -- nothing resets last_raw at the start of a pass. _debug_capture: `record = self.capture_record()` / `raw = record.get("raw")` -> written as the entry's raw. byte14_probe final pass: `scanner.scan(resolution=args.resolution, ..., keep_raw=False, byte14=None)` after a keep_raw=True ladder at the same resolution/frame. library.save performs no layout-vs-image check.
findings.description: CLAUDE.md requires RPS7200_DEBUG=1 for every ad-hoc script, and prescan() defaults keep_raw=False. A keep_raw=False pass is filed either without raw bytes (contrary to 'file every scan with its raw bytes') or, after any keep_raw=True pass (every auto_exposure probe is one), with that earlier pass's bytes and layout. When shapes match nothing detects it.
findings.failure_scenario: RPS7200_DEBUG=1 tools/byte14_probe.py: the final default-byte14 pass is filed with the last ladder pass's raw.bin.gz (same shape). reconstruct reports 'decode CHANGED x% differ'; `tools/library.py migrate-raw --write` then overwrites the correct scan.tif with the other pass's decode, destroying the only true pixels.
findings.recommendation: Set self.last_raw = self.last_raw_layout = None at the top of scan(); force keep_raw=True whenever self.debug; validate raw.layout (lines/width/channels) against the image in library.save and refuse mismatches; make migrate-raw verify the stored image is a correction of the decode before rewriting.

findings.title: `tools/library.py duplicates --delete` deletes scans of different photographs when film notes are empty
findings.evidence: signature returns (stock, frame, subject, resolution_dpi, channels, frame window, depth, film, protocol_revision, commanded, fast_infrared) -- no time, transport position, roll index or content. tools/library.py: `if args.delete: shutil.rmtree(path)`. Debug entries use `FilmNotes(notes="captured with RPS7200_DEBUG on")`; GUI entries use _notes() which is empty unless typed; roll frames use `frame=job.notes.frame or f"{name}-{number:02d}"`.
findings.description: The docstring assumes equal signatures mean 'the same scan of the same picture', but every GUI prescan, GUI single scan and debug entry of the same settings with empty stock/frame/subject shares one signature. If the operator types anything into the GUI 'frame' field, every frame of a roll gets the same film.frame and the whole roll collapses too.
findings.failure_scenario: Ten GUI prescans of ten different frames at 300 dpi, or twenty debug prescans from a transport probe, are reported as 'redundant' and `--delete` rmtree's all but the newest -- exactly the 'two entries from different frames' evidence CLAUDE.md says settles sensor-vs-picture questions.
findings.recommendation: Only treat entries as duplicates when stock and frame are non-empty and roll_position/transport position match; add a content check (e.g. correlation of prescan/scan thumbnails); ask for confirmation and move to a trash folder instead of rmtree.

findings.title: approved.json is written to a different folder than the roll it belongs to
findings.evidence: gui `_write_approved`: `name = _safe(self.fields["roll"].get().strip())` / `folder = Path(self.session.rolls) / name`. session._roll: `name = job.name or time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")` / `out = Path(job.out) if job.out else self.rolls / name`. `_safe("")` returns "roll". open_roll never sets fields["roll"].
findings.description: The operator's committed positions/turns -- which the code calls the one thing not derivable from the library -- are filed under a recomputed, sanitised name while the roll writes under the raw name or today's date. session.last_roll_dir exists precisely to avoid recomputing this and is not used.
findings.failure_scenario: Default empty roll name: the walk and roll go to rolls/2026-09-23/, approved.json to rolls/roll/approved.json (overwritten by the next commission of any unnamed roll). Reopening 2026-09-23 shows no committed positions. A name like 'Gold 200' splits into rolls/Gold 200/ and rolls/Gold-200/. Reopening an old walk and pressing 'Scan chosen' with the field empty scans into today's folder, so the old walk never gains its roll.json.
findings.recommendation: Write approved.json into self._sheet_roll / session.last_roll_dir (or pass it with the Roll and let _roll write it into `out`); set the roll-name field from the folder in open_roll; sanitise the name once in session._roll with the same _safe.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/session.py:1147-1152 'so a caller that wants to file something beside that manifest -- the contact sheet's decisions ... can ask rather than recompute the same name and drift out of step with it'

findings.title: tools/scan_roll.py overwrites roll.json when a roll is resumed
findings.evidence: scan_roll.py builds `manifest = {"roll": roll_name, ..., "held": held_note, "frames": []}` and checkpoint() does `manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, ...))`; no existing manifest is read. The GUI path reads `earlier` and merges `"frames": list(earlier.get("frames") or [])`.
findings.description: The CLI resume path starts a new manifest and replaces the previous run's frame records (registration, exposure, entry paths, done flags) with only the frames of the new run; the GUI path merges.
findings.failure_scenario: A 24-frame roll dies at frame 11; `scan_roll.py --roll X --start-at 12` rewrites rolls/X/roll.json with frames 12-24 only; the record of frames 1-11 and their library entry paths is gone and the GUI then offers 1-11 as unscanned.
findings.recommendation: Reuse session._roll's merge (renumbered + replace-by-number) in the CLI, or route the CLI through ScanSession.
findings.doc_reference: README.md:547-549 'a resumed roll carries forward what the earlier session already did instead of overwriting its manifest'; tools/scan_roll.py:23-24 '`--start-at` resumes from the manifest'

findings.title: CLI dry-run walks file nothing in the library; prescans exist only as corrected TIFFs in the roll folder
findings.evidence: scan_roll.py dry-run branch: `pre = out / f"prescan{number:02d}.tif"` / `tiff.write(str(pre), frame.prescan)` -- no writer.submit, frame.raw_prescan and capture unused. GUI dry run: `self._file(seq, number, rf.prescan, ..., raw_image=rf.raw_prescan, path=surveyed, ...)`.
findings.description: The walk's prescans are the evidence positions are proposed from, yet the CLI keeps neither raw bytes, raw pixels, reference nor mask for them. GUI and CLI diverge. The GUI's roll-delete dialog tells the operator everything but approved.json is re-derivable from the library, which is false for CLI walks.
findings.failure_scenario: A 38-frame CLI walk followed by deleting its roll folder (or a detector change needing the raw prescans) loses every prescan irrecoverably.
findings.recommendation: In the dry-run branch submit each prescan to FrameWriter with raw_image=frame.raw_prescan, meta=frame.prescan_meta and capture=s.capture_record(), as session._roll does.
findings.doc_reference: tools/gui.py:2487-2490 'Everything in a roll folder is re-derivable from the library **except `approved.json`**'

findings.title: A frame's prescan is stored corrected and unlabelled; arrival and verification prescans of held frames are never kept
findings.evidence: `prescan=rf.prescan,` (corrected) while rf.raw_prescan is not passed; library.save writes `tiff.write(str(path / "prescan.tif"), prescan)` and the prescan record has only file/read_direction/carriage_state. In the held branch `prescan_image = fix["prescan"]` replaces the arrival prescan without setting prescan_before; `_hold_to_approved` keeps only the last verification pass.
findings.description: prescan.tif in a frame entry is the only record of the framing pass on a real roll, but it is corrected with today's reference, carries no raw bytes and no 300 dpi mask, and nothing says it is corrected. The prescan the frame arrived at and all intermediate hold-loop passes are discarded (prescan_before is only written on dry runs and only for _aim_frame).
findings.failure_scenario: A held frame lands badly; there is no stored picture of where it arrived or of the intermediate moves to check the hold loop against, and the stored prescan cannot be re-corrected.
findings.recommendation: File every prescan/verification pass as its own entry (raw) linked from the frame record by id, or store raw_prescan + its mask + raw bytes in the frame entry and mark prescan corrections; set prescan_before in the held branch too.

findings.title: Roll and hold-loop prescans record film 'negative' whatever the roll's film
findings.evidence: prescan(..., film: str = FILM_NEGATIVE); scan_roll: `prescan_image, _ = self.prescan(resolution=prescan_resolution, keep_raw=keep_raw)`; _hold_to_approved: `image, _ = self.prescan(resolution=prescan_resolution, keep_raw=keep_raw)`.
findings.description: prescan_meta therefore says film='negative' for B&W/slide rolls, and GUI dry-run prescan entries are filed with scan.film='negative'. library.signature and the demo's picture selection key on scan.film.
findings.failure_scenario: A B&W walk's prescan entries claim colour negative; the demo shows them for negative strips; signature groups them with negative prescans.
findings.recommendation: Pass film through scan_roll -> prescan and _hold_to_approved/_aim_frame.

findings.title: 7200 dpi scan.tif is realigned but the record does not say so; reconstruct and migrate-raw can never validate it
findings.evidence: `if resolution == self.NATIVE_COLUMN_STAGGER_DPI: ... image = self._realign_native_column_stagger(image)` (only a log line) then `raw_pixels = image`. reconstruct uses `DirectScanner.decode_index(raw, params, ...)` with no realignment and returns `decode CHANGED: now {image.shape}, stored {stored.shape}`.
findings.description: scan.tif at 7200 dpi is decode + stagger realignment (4 rows trimmed, odd columns shifted), not 'the decode alone'. No meta field records the transform, reconstruct reports every such entry as a changed decode, migrate-raw marks it failed, and in ScanSession the lines guard drops the raw bytes altogether.
findings.failure_scenario: `scan.py --dpi 7200 --no-shading` entries show '!' in every `make reconstruct` run; a genuine regression at 7200 dpi is indistinguishable; a GUI/API 7200 dpi pass through ScanSession is filed without raw bytes.
findings.recommendation: Record `realigned_lines` in meta and apply the same step in reconstruct/decode_raw (one shared decode_for_entry), or store the plain decode and realign in library.corrected.

findings.title: ScanSession guard drops the raw bytes of a short read, the case where they matter most
findings.evidence: `actual = {"lines": shape[0], ...}` compared with `layout["lines"]` (= params.lines); on disagreement `capture = dict(capture, raw=None, raw_path=None, raw_layout=None)` -- reference and ccd_mask kept. read_planes: `except EndOfData: ... break`; decode: `height = min(len(planes[c]) for c in order)`.
findings.description: A pass that ended early (EndOfData) decodes to fewer rows than layout['lines'], so its genuine bytes are discarded and the entry cannot be re-decoded. Conversely when raw really belongs to another pass the guard keeps that pass's mask. tools/scan_roll.py has no guard at all, so the two paths file differently.
findings.failure_scenario: A frame truncated by the scanner mid-roll is filed without raw.bin.gz; the diagnosis of why it was short is impossible.
findings.recommendation: Compare against layout['lines_received'] / the decode of the bytes rather than params.lines; when raw is dropped also drop mask/reference unless they are known to belong to this pass; share one guard between GUI and CLI.

findings.title: library.save discards inquiry, caller meta and capture time; scan() does not record protocol overrides
findings.evidence: save(..., inquiry: Any = None, ...) never uses `inquiry`; `when = datetime.now(timezone.utc)` at filing; scan block is a fixed key whitelist. Dropped: meta['bracket_index'/'bracket_ratio'/'bracket_passes'/'bracket_stops'], meta['roll_index'], meta['roll_position'], meta['uniformity_session'], meta['demo']. scan() never records `byte14`, `slide_init_param`, `skip_shading`, the base Settings before scaling, `available_lines`. _debug_capture stores `"captured": time.time()` and never passes it on.
findings.description: Several parameters needed to re-evaluate a scan are silently lost between the pass and the entry, and 'created' is the filing time (minutes to hours later for debug flushes and queued frames).
findings.failure_scenario: The byte14 ladder's entries (the probe requires debug filing) do not say which byte14 each pass used; bracket members cannot be regrouped; roll frames do not record their transport position; firmware/model of the scanner is not recorded.
findings.recommendation: Store unknown meta keys verbatim under scan.extra, record inquiry fields, the MODE SELECT/GAIN payload bytes actually sent, and a captured_at timestamp taken in scan().

findings.title: GUI single scans gzip their raw bytes while the device is open and idle
findings.evidence: FrameWriter docstring: 'On this thread the write instead overlaps the next frame's scan, so the device is busy rather than idle throughout.' After _scan returns, the worker blocks in `job = self._jobs.get()` with the scanner open while FrameWriter runs library.save -> gzip.
findings.description: For a roll the gzip overlaps the next pass; for a single GUI scan or prescan there is no next pass, so the device sits open and idle for the whole gzip -- the state CLAUDE.md says preceded a wedge. The window keeps the device open for its whole lifetime.
findings.failure_scenario: A 3600 dpi RGBI single scan (~250 MB raw) is gzipped for tens of seconds with the device open and idle between jobs.
findings.recommendation: Spool uncompressed during the session and gzip after close, use a fast/no compression level while open, or close/re-open the device around single-scan filing; at least measure it with tools/filing_load_test.py.
findings.doc_reference: CLAUDE.md:155-158 '**A single scan compresses nothing while the device is open.** ... gzipping one with the scanner open and idle preceded a wedge once.'

findings.title: Manifests and entry records are written non-atomically; a corrupt roll.json is silently discarded on resume
findings.evidence: `try: earlier = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(...)) except (OSError, ValueError): earlier = {}` then the manifest is rewritten with `manifest_path.write_text(...)`. library.save/migrations use write_text / tiff.write in place. settings.save by contrast uses a .part file and replace().
findings.description: A crash or power loss during a write truncates roll.json/survey.json/scan.json/scan.tif. On the next resume the GUI treats the unreadable manifest as empty and overwrites it, losing every earlier frame record without a word.
findings.failure_scenario: Machine crashes while roll.json is being rewritten after frame 20; resume reads {} and writes a manifest containing only the new frames.
findings.recommendation: Write via temp file + os.replace everywhere (as settings.save does); refuse to resume (or back up) when an existing manifest cannot be parsed.

findings.title: scan_roll.py: Ctrl-C abandons the read and skips writer.finish(), losing queued frames
findings.evidence: `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001` then `writer.finish()`; the comment at 598 says 'Reached through a `finally` around the whole scanning block, so it runs whatever came out of it.' scan(): `except BaseException: self._scanning = False; raise`.
findings.description: KeyboardInterrupt is not an Exception, so it unwinds past writer.finish(); the daemon FrameWriter thread is killed at exit with up to three frames unfiled, the manifest never gets finished/stopped, and the read in flight is abandoned (wedge). Neither CLI tool handles SIGINT.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator hits Ctrl-C to stop a roll: scanner needs a power cycle and the last 1-3 scanned frames never reach the library.
findings.recommendation: Use try/finally for writer.finish and the final checkpoint; install a SIGINT handler that sets should_stop so the roll ends at the next safe point.
findings.doc_reference: tools/scan_roll.py:598 'Reached through a `finally` around the whole scanning block'

findings.title: A second walk into the same roll folder overwrites survey.json and the prescans
findings.evidence: Default name `time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")`; `manifest_path = out / ("survey.json" if job.dry_run else "roll.json")` and `earlier` is only read `if not job.dry_run`; prescans are written to `out / f"prescan{number:02d}.tif"` (no _unclaimed).
findings.description: Walking twice on one day with the default name (or reusing a name) replaces the first walk's survey and prescan files; walked_prescans' docstring already documents the confusion this causes. approved.json from an earlier commission then refers to other pictures.
findings.failure_scenario: Morning walk of strip A, afternoon walk of strip B, both unnamed: strip A's survey.json and prescanNN.tif are overwritten; reopening the folder shows B with A's approvals.
findings.recommendation: Refuse or version an existing survey (survey-2.json / new folder), or warn in the Roll dialog when the folder already holds a walk.

findings.title: The roll keyboard shortcut bypasses the busy guard, and any submit clears a pending stop
findings.evidence: `"roll": self.on_roll,` (prescan/scan keys go through _confirm_then which checks self.busy; roll does not). on_roll comment: 'The button this handler is behind is disabled while busy, so this cannot race a job that is still running.' submit(): `self._stop.clear(); self._jobs.put(job)`.
findings.description: While a walk or roll is running, the roll key opens the Roll dialog; confirming a dry run clears self.survey, sheet_state and restarts edge_watch, and the submit clears a Stop the operator already requested, so the running job continues and a second roll is queued.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator presses Stop, then the roll key by mistake and OK: the current walk does not stop, its surveyed frames vanish from the sheet, and another walk starts after it.
findings.recommendation: Check self.busy in on_roll (and every handler reachable by key); only clear _stop when the worker takes the next job (it already does in _run).

findings.title: DemoScanner runs its own roll loop that diverges from DirectScanner.scan_roll
findings.evidence: demo: `fix = self._hold_to_approved(index, prescan, 300, held, keep_raw=False, reverse=reverse_hold,)` (no should_stop, prescan dpi fixed 300); `marks["base"] = walk.observe(index, prescan)` only in the `elif walk is not None` branch; loop body is `try: ... finally: self._frame_source = None` with no except; `yield RollFrame(index=..., image=image, meta=meta or {}, prescan=prescan, registration=marks, prescan_meta=prescan_meta)`.
findings.description: The real loop catches UsbError/ScanReadError/ShadingUnavailable/ValueError per frame and yields an error frame up to max_failures, observes every frame before holding, honours prescan_resolution/meter/blank_contrast/should_stop in the hold, and yields raw_image/raw_prescan/prescan_before and meta['registration']. None of that runs in the demo, so the failed-frame path, the StripWalk state with held frames and the raw filing of roll frames are untested with no device.
findings.failure_scenario: A demo roll with approvals never feeds held frames to StripWalk; a demo frame error ends the whole roll instead of being recorded as not done; demo roll entries have no registration record.
findings.recommendation: Move the loop into one place (e.g. a module-level roll driver parameterised by prescan/scan/advance/nudge primitives) and have DemoScanner supply only the primitives.

findings.title: Demo passes return corrected pixels without last_pixels_raw, ignore shading=False and 7200 dpi refusals, and leave stale calibration in the capture
findings.evidence: _decode: `if reference is not None and not (...).get("skipped"): image, self._shading_report = apply_shading(image, reference, mask)` regardless of the pass's shading flag; prescan's prescan.tif branch returns `tiff.read(str(tif))` without touching self._capture; no attribute last_pixels_raw is ever set; scan() has no MAX_SHADING_COLUMNS check; ensure_shading returns `"loaded" if reuse` without a file.
findings.description: Through the unchanged session path, demo scans and prescans are filed with corrected pixels as raw, with the source entry's raw bytes (when shapes match) and a reference/mask that may belong to a previous decode at another resolution. A 7200 dpi pass the scanner refuses before any bytes move succeeds in the demo; shading=False still yields corrected pixels.
findings.failure_scenario: In --demo, prescan after a 1800 dpi scan: the demo/library prescan entry carries the 1800 dpi pass's ccd_mask.bin and shading.npz; library.corrected applies that mask to a 300 dpi image (wrong columns) on top of pixels that were already corrected; reconstruct flags every demo entry.
findings.recommendation: Give DemoScanner last_pixels_raw (the uncorrected decode), reset _capture on every pass, apply DirectScanner's width refusal via a shared static, honour shading=False, and have reuse fail over to 'calibrated' when no cache exists.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/demo.py:15-20 'decoding it here runs the same `_deinterleave` and the same shading correction a real pass runs, and `capture_record` can hand the session genuine bytes to file. An entry the demo files reconstructs like any other.'

findings.title: Demo scan ignores the simulated film position; backlash constant retyped
findings.evidence: prescan: `image, read = self._read_as_carriage(self._as_positioned(image), ONE_PASS_COLOR)`; scan: `image = self._pair_image("scan.tif", film, resolution)` with no _as_positioned. Backlash: `swallowed = min(abs(asked), 2.2 * 0.1057)`.
findings.description: After the hold loop moves the simulated film, the demo's frame scan still shows the unmoved picture, so the scan disagrees with its own prescan (and _note_reversal compares mismatched pictures). 0.1057 is protocol.MM_PER_UNIT retyped, against the 'taken from DirectScanner, never retyped' rule.
findings.failure_scenario: Demo roll with an approved offset: the delivered frame is not re-centred although the log says it was held.
findings.recommendation: Apply _as_positioned (scaled to the scan's dpi) in scan(); use protocol.MM_PER_UNIT.

findings.title: verify says 'correction was asked for' about deliberately raw scans
findings.evidence: `why = cal.get("skipped")` / `f"corrected" + (f" -- correction was asked for: {why}" if why else "")` -- fires for SHADING_SKIPPED_EXPLICIT too.
findings.description: verify does not distinguish the explicit shading=False reason from a shortfall; every --no-shading entry is reported as a correction that was wanted.
findings.failure_scenario: `make verify` after `scan.py --no-shading` prints 'no shading reference ... -- correction was asked for: shading=False (explicit)'.
findings.recommendation: Compare against SHADING_SKIPPED_EXPLICIT in verify as corrected() does.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/library.py:362 '`verify` already draws that line and calls the other one "a thing that went wrong"'; direct.py:300-301

findings.title: The comparison files do not exercise the driver's correction path
findings.evidence: `raw = tiff.read(scan_path)` (default scans/negatives/state_1800dpi.tif), `corrected = destripe(raw, defects, margin=12, dilate=5)`; no library entry, raw bytes, shading.npz or apply_shading is used; writes previews/*.png into a directory it does not create.
findings.description: CLAUDE.md makes these three files the eye-check after any change to the scan or correction path, but 2_corrected.tif is a flat-based destripe of an arbitrary TIFF, not library.corrected() of a stored scan, so a regression in apply_shading/decode would not appear.
findings.failure_scenario: A change breaks apply_shading; the regenerated comparison files look unchanged and are sent as evidence.
findings.recommendation: Build 1/2/3 from a library entry: decode_raw (1), library.corrected (2), invert (3).
findings.doc_reference: CLAUDE.md:179-183 'Regenerate the three comparison files after any significant change to the scan or correction path'

findings.title: scan_roll.py --approved does not un-orient GUI walk prescans
findings.evidence: CLI: `frames = [(number, tiff.read(str(path))) for number, path, _ in walked_prescans(...)]` used directly as Approved.reference. GUI: `turn = int(manifest.get("rotation") or 0)` ... `image=preview.unorient(image, turn, mirrored)`.
findings.description: GUI walks write prescanNN.tif arranged by the session rotation/flip and record it in survey.json; the CLI proposes positions and correlates fresh (unrotated) prescans against the rotated references.
findings.failure_scenario: A strip walked in the window with 'rotate 180' then commissioned via `scan_roll.py --approved rolls/X`: edge proposals are mirrored and measure_shift_mm aims frames the wrong way or abstains.
findings.recommendation: Apply preview.unorient with the manifest's rotation/flipped in hold_from_walk (share read_survey's code).

findings.title: GUI roll export cannot find CLI-scanned roll entries (film.frame join key differs)
findings.evidence: CLI: `frame=f"{roll_name}/{number:02d}"`; GUI: `frame=job.notes.frame or f"{name}-{number:02d}"`; roll_entry_index: `roll, _, number = frame.rpartition("-")` / `if not roll or not number.isdigit(): continue`.
findings.description: The join between roll folders and library entries relies on a string format the two writers do not share (and on the operator leaving the frame field empty).
findings.failure_scenario: Export of a CLI-scanned roll from the roll browser says no frame has a library entry left.
findings.recommendation: Record the library entry id in roll.json per frame (the CLI already does after finish) and join on it; use one frame-label format.

findings.title: --look-only without --demo drives the real scanner while the window says there is no film
findings.evidence: `no_film=args.look_only` reaches only DemoScanner; the sheet text says 'There is no film in the transport ... Scanning is offered as it always is, and will say there is no film when it reaches for it.'
findings.description: With a real scanner nothing refuses, so the controls move film and scan.
findings.failure_scenario: `gui.py --look-only --open-roll X` with the scanner attached: pressing 'Scan chosen' seeks, calibrates and scans for real.
findings.recommendation: Reject --look-only without --demo, or make ScanSession refuse transport jobs when look_only is set.

findings.title: README describes reversal-by-prescan turning that the code no longer does
findings.evidence: _note_reversal: `if _read_known(meta): ... return meta` -- a pass whose line tags gave a direction is never turned; only unknown-direction passes are judged by picture.
findings.description: The README still presents picture comparison against the prescan as the mechanism.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator expects a mismatched frame to be turned automatically; it is only logged.
findings.recommendation: Update README to describe line-tag direction and the log-only disagreement.
findings.doc_reference: README.md:352-358 'A pass that comes back the wrong way up is turned to match its prescan ... The only evidence is that the picture does not match the framing pass'

findings.title: Transport-distance documentation disagrees with the code and with itself
findings.evidence: MM_PER_UNIT = 0.1057, COMMAND_UNITS = 1.84, MM_PER_COMMAND = MM_PER_UNIT * COMMAND_UNITS (0.1945 mm); FULL_FRAME width 10344 -> 345.2 units. Code, CLI (--nudge mm, prints mm) and approved.json (offset_mm) are in millimetres.
findings.description: README states the old ramp; CLAUDE.md gives two values for param 1 and for the aperture; CLAUDE.md prohibits millimetres while every stored offset is in mm.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone checks a move against README's 0.1662 mm or CLAUDE.md's 2.6 units and sees a discrepancy that is in the docs.
findings.recommendation: Align README/CLAUDE.md with protocol.py (param+1.84 units, 2.84 for param 1, aperture 345.2) and either store units or document that storage stays in mm.
findings.doc_reference: README.md:554-556 'move `0.1057 × param + 0.1662` mm'; CLAUDE.md:420 '`param 1` (~2.6 units)' vs CLAUDE.md:265 '2.84'; CLAUDE.md:460 'against 344.5' vs CLAUDE.md:264 '345.2'; CLAUDE.md:245 'Millimetres are prohibited.'

findings.title: 'File every scan' is not true of the tools or the window: metering probes and hold passes are never filed, even with RPS7200_DEBUG=1
findings.evidence: `DirectScanner(verbose=self.verbose, debug=False)`; `DirectScanner(verbose=args.verbose, debug=False)`; `self.debug = (os.environ.get(...) ... if debug is None else bool(debug))` -- an explicit False overrides the environment. auto_exposure comments that probes use keep_raw=True because 'CLAUDE.md's rule is "file every scan, with its raw bytes"', yet nothing files them.
findings.description: Every metering probe (2-3 per metered frame), every hold-loop verification prescan and the arrival prescan of held frames are discarded in the GUI and both CLI tools; setting RPS7200_DEBUG=1 does not change that.
findings.failure_scenario: After a 38-frame metered roll about 100 probe passes and every hold verification exist nowhere; a question about metering or a bad hold cannot be answered from stored data.
findings.recommendation: Let the tools/session file probe and verification passes through FrameWriter (tagged 'probe'/'hold') when debug is on, or honour the env var over the explicit False.
findings.doc_reference: CLAUDE.md:104 '**File every scan in the library, with its raw bytes.**' and CLAUDE.md:137-146 (env var 'better because a script inherits it')

findings.title: Debug spool is unrecoverable after a hard kill: metadata, layout and calibration live only in memory
findings.evidence: _debug_capture writes only `np.save(image_path, image)` and `raw_path.write_bytes(raw)`; `item = {"meta": dict(meta), ...}`, raw_layout, reference and ccd_mask are appended to `self._debug_pending` in memory; filing happens only in close() -> _debug_flush.
findings.description: The spool exists to survive long sessions, but a process killed by the 10-minute harness limit, a crash or a hung wedge never reaches close(); the orphaned .npy/.bin files carry no meta, no layout and no reference and there is no recovery command.
findings.failure_scenario: A probe runs past 10 minutes in the foreground and is killed: every pass of the session is lost as library entries although the pixels sit in $TMP.
findings.recommendation: Write a JSON sidecar (meta, layout), shading npz and mask per spooled item, and add `tools/library.py recover-spool`.

findings.title: scan.py --bracket silently ignores a single-value --exposure-scale
findings.evidence: `exposure_scale = parts[0] if len(parts) == 1 else parts` (float); bracket: `exposure_scale=(list(exposure_scale) if isinstance(exposure_scale, list) else None)` and `auto_exposure=args.auto_exposure and not args.exposure_scale` -> False, so scan_bracket uses `scales = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]`.
findings.description: The requested fixed exposure is dropped with no message; the single-pass path honours it.
findings.failure_scenario: `scan.py --bracket 5 --exposure-scale 2` brackets around the device default instead of x2.
findings.recommendation: Pass [x]*3 for a scalar.

findings.title: 7200 dpi is offered but always refused, and a roll only refuses after prescan, metering and holds
findings.evidence: `self._int(self.v_dpi, "Scan dpi", 25, 7200)`; scan(): `if needed > self.MAX_SHADING_COLUMNS: raise ShadingUnavailable(...)`; the window never sends shading=False; scan_roll checks film/infrared up front but not the shading width, and catches ShadingUnavailable per frame.
findings.description: A single 7200 dpi scan fails immediately (cheap), but a 7200 dpi roll prescans, meters, nudges and then fails each frame until max_failures.
findings.failure_scenario: A 7200 dpi roll moves film and spends ~1 min per frame for three frames before giving up.
findings.recommendation: Refuse up front in scan_roll (same static check) and in the dialogs, or drop 7200 from the resolution list.

findings.title: No checksums for shading.npz, ccd_mask.bin or prescan.tif
findings.evidence: Only image.sha256 and raw.sha256 are recorded; verify only checks existence of `cal.get(key)` files.
findings.description: Corruption of the calibration or mask, which decide every corrected pixel, is not detectable by verify.
findings.failure_scenario: A bit flip in shading.npz changes every future library.corrected() output; verify reports the library intact.
findings.recommendation: Record and verify sha256 for every file in the entry.

findings.title: Calibrate button starts a calibration without asking whether film is loaded
findings.evidence: `def on_calibrate(...): self.session.submit(Calibrate(mode=mode or self.v_shading.get(), reference=self.session.reference))` with no confirmation.
findings.description: CLAUDE.md records that calibrating an empty transport preceded a wedge and that only Stefan can see the transport; the main-window button does not ask.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator calibrates right after power-on with the strip still out.
findings.recommendation: Ask 'Is the film loaded?' before a measured calibration (the prompt path could carry the same question).

findings.title: Library, calibration cache and roll paths are relative to the current directory
findings.evidence: `DEFAULT_ROOT = Path("library")`; ScanSession(root="library", reference="calibration/shading.npz", rolls="rolls"); gui `home = DEMO_ROOT if args.demo else Path(".")`.
findings.description: Launching a tool from another directory silently starts a new library, cache and rolls tree there; `--demo --library library` files demo entries into the real library with no 'demo' marker (meta['demo'] is not whitelisted).
findings.failure_scenario: `cd tools && uv run python gui.py` files scans into tools/library/, invisible to `make reconstruct`.
findings.recommendation: Resolve defaults against the repository/ a configured data root; record meta['demo'] and refuse demo filing into a non-demo library.

findings.title: Quitting mid-roll waits for the whole roll and every queued job
findings.evidence: on_close: 'Quitting waits for it to finish' then `self.session.shutdown()` which only puts None at the end of the job queue; no request_stop.
findings.description: The dialog reads as 'wait for this pass', but the window stays until the whole roll (hours) and any queued jobs finish.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator closes the window 3 frames into a 38-frame roll expecting it to stop after the pass.
findings.recommendation: Offer 'stop after this frame and quit' (request_stop + shutdown) alongside 'wait for the roll'.

findings.title: Layering: library depends on direct, with a lazy import cycle back
findings.evidence: library: `from .direct import SHADING_SKIPPED_EXPLICIT, DirectScanner, ScanParameters`; direct._debug_flush: `from . import library`; demo: `from .session import estimate_seconds`; gui imports session's private `_safe`, `_unclaimed`.
findings.description: The offline data layer needs the device module for a constant and the static decode; the decode used by reconstruct/demo is reached through DirectScanner rather than a decode module, which is also why the 7200 realignment in scan() is invisible to reconstruct.
findings.recommendation: Move decode_index/realignment/SHADING_SKIPPED_EXPLICIT into a small decode module used by direct, library and demo.
